home.title: TB Config Studio
home.intro: Explains and edits the config files of the TheModBase (TB) mods for DayZ servers. Everything stays on this PC.
home.openHelp: Pick the profile folder of your DayZ server: the folder that contains TBMods (with TBMods\Config inside). A server folder that contains profile folders works too.
home.typePath: Type or choose a folder first.
home.severalBody: Pick the one you want to open.
first.title: First run guide
first.1: Start your server once with the TB mods installed. Each mod writes its config files the first time it runs.
first.2: Stop the server before you edit. The TB mods read their configs only when the server starts, so a change needs a restart.
first.3: Open the server profile folder here (the folder that contains TBMods). The mods that have configs there appear in the overview.
first.4: Open a mod, read the explanation next to each field, change what you need, then use Review and save. You see exactly what changes before anything is written.
first.5: Every save keeps a backup. If something goes wrong, use Backups and rollback to put an older version back.
first.done: Got it, hide this on the start page

pre.suggestionBody: They are starting points collected by the app's author, not official settings of the mod author. You see every change as a diff before anything is applied, and a backup is made first.

lic.title: Licence helper
lic.intro: Each TB mod needs a licence for the server it runs on. This page shows what the app can see on this PC and walks you through the usual causes of the "Your Server is deactivated" message. It reads no licence content and talks to no website.
lic.fact: A licence belongs to one server, identified by its public IP address and its game port as they are registered on the TB website. If the server answers from another address or port than the one registered, the check fails.
lic.noPort: Not found. DayZ usually takes the game port from the -port= start parameter, not from serverDZ.cfg. Check your start script.
lic.filesNote: Only the presence of the file for each mod is checked.
lic.checklistIntro: Work through these from top to bottom and restart the server after each fix.
lic.c1: The licence file of each mod is in the profile folder under TheModBase\Licenses (one file per mod, named after the mod).
lic.c2: On the TB website the server is registered with the public IP address your players connect to, and each mod licence is assigned to that server.
lic.c3: The game port you registered is the port the server really runs on (the -port= start parameter).
lic.c4: Your public IP has not changed since you registered it (home connections and some hosts change it). Update it on the website if it did.
lic.c5: If the PC has both IPv4 and IPv6, the check may use the wrong one. On one test server, setting TheModBase\Config\IPSettings.txt to the word ipv4 fixed this.
lic.c6: The mod itself and TBLib are loaded by the server (the server-side files of every licensed mod are in the server's mod list).
lic.c7: The profile folder you started the server with is the one that holds the licences (the -profiles= start parameter).
lic.c8: Check the server log for messages from the TB mods right after start, they say which check failed.
bk.title: Backups and rollback
bk.intro: A backup of a file is made every time this app writes to it. Pick one to see what restoring it would change.
pk.title: Config packs
pk.intro: A pack is a plain folder copy of config files that you can copy, store or share. Importing shows what would change first.
pk.exportHelp: Choose the mods, then a new empty folder. The pack keeps the same folder layout as a profile (TBMods\Config\…).
pk.strip: Remove secrets from the copy (webhook addresses, keys, Steam ids)
pk.importHelp: Pick a pack folder (or another server profile). Only the files you tick are written, each with a backup first.
pk.importBody: Existing files are backed up first. The server needs a restart to use them.
guide.title: Guide
guide.g1.b: Each mod creates its configs in TBMods\Config when the server first starts with it, and reads them again only at the next start. Edit with the server stopped, then start it. Some mods also have an admin reload in game, check the mod's own documentation.
guide.g2.b: Before each write the app copies the current file to its backup folder, then writes the new file in one step so a crash cannot leave half a file. If the file changed on disk after you opened it, the app tells you instead of overwriting silently. Only the values you change are rewritten: comments, spacing and the order of keys stay as they were.
guide.g3.t: Fields the app does not know
guide.g3.b: A mod update may add settings. They are always shown, marked not described, and can be edited as plain values. Nothing is hidden because the app has no description for it.
guide.g4.b: Webhook addresses, keys, tokens and Steam ids are hidden in the window. You can type a new value to replace one. Steam ids used as names show only their last four digits.
guide.g5.b: Many TB configs refer to other files by name, for example a trader list naming files in the DealerPoints folder, or reward levels naming reward files. Keep the spelling and capital letters exactly equal to the file name without .json.
guide.g6.b: Presets are suggestions, not official values. The default values shown next to fields come from real files written by the mod versions listed under Mods and schemas, so a newer version may differ.
covw.title: Mods and schemas
covw.intro: How well the app knows each mod. In depth means every field was checked against real config files and the public documentation. Partly or inferred means some or all explanations come from field names and real files only.
covw.add: Add or update a mod description
covw.addBody: Descriptions are plain JSON files. Put a file into the schemas-user folder in the app's data folder (see docs/SCHEMA-FORMAT.md), then reload. A file there replaces the built-in description of the same mod.
